thread:
ash: Heads up — saw repeated AccessDenied in prod when a Lambda with an assumed role tries to decrypt payloads. Happens right after key rotation window. Anyone seen this pattern? :grimacing:

ash: Stack trace from the Lambda logs:
```
2025-09-03T14:02:11Z ERROR KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::222233334444:assumed-role/infra-deploy-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234-efgh-5678
    Status code: 400, Request ID: 8f9a-...
```

maya: :eyes: can you paste the key policy? my first guess is a Principal/Condition mismatch (aws:SourceAccount / aws:PrincipalArn) that blocks the assumed-role session ARN rather than the role principal itself.

ash: snippet of the key policy we found attached to the CMK:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowOrgUsage",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/encryptor" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/encryptor" } }
}
```

kevin: yep that's the culprit. when a role is assumed the principal making the KMS call is the assumed-role session ARN (arn:aws:sts::222233334444:assumed-role/infra-deploy-role/session). The condition on aws:PrincipalArn will fail. Two options: (1) change key policy to allow the role principal (i.e., the role ARN) without matching the session ARN or remove that restriction, or (2) add the assumed-role session ARN(s) explicitly (not ideal).

jordan: also verify EncryptionContext. If the Decrypt request includes an EncryptionContext and it doesn't match the one used for GenerateDataKey/Encrypt, KMS will deny. Quick check with CloudTrail: find the kms:Decrypt event and look at requestParameters.encryptionContext.

sec-bot: CloudTrail KMS event lookup: found event where ErrorCode = "AccessDeniedException" and userIdentity.principalId = "AIDA:assumed-role/infra-deploy-role:session". Request contained encryptionContext = {"purpose":"envelope"}.

kevin: FYI: IAM policy on the role granting kms:Decrypt won't help if key policy denies — make sure the key policy allows the role. Grants can also be used: issuing a KMS grant to the role ARN would permit use even if key policy is restrictive, but grants are short-lived and per-key.

ash: we tried adding kms:Decrypt to the role's inline policy earlier (no effect). after removing the aws:PrincipalArn condition from the key policy and replacing with a Principal that includes "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/encryptor" and the aws:SourceAccount condition instead, the Lambda decrypts succeeded in canary.

maya: good catch. For cross-account roles, prefer Principal + SourceAccount conditions instead of matching the session ARN. Also document this in the KB: note about assumed-role session vs role ARN and common encryptionContext pitfalls.

ash: thanks — i'll open a tiny PR to update the key policy templates and add an entry to runbook: check key policy principal vs assumed-role session + check CloudTrail encryptionContext.
